title: Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) durian (Duyaya): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) durian is a durian variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) is a registered durian variety, also sold or known as Duyaya or Duyaya durian. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1999 as NSIC 1999 Dr 06. Severino Belviz bred it. Its record notes a yield of 45 to 50 fruits.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) was about 6 years old and about 6 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 45 to 50 fruits. It bears regularly, with fruit in August October. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) weighs about 5071 grams, and its shape is oblong w/ characteristics beak at styral end. The flesh is bright yellow and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 31.69 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 30.25 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is August October, bearing regular.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Oblong with a beak at the tip, about 5 kg, brown, bright yellow, smooth, firm flesh, strong aroma, 31.7 Brix, about 30 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a big, very sweet Calinan durian (about 5 kg, 31.7 Brix) with a strong aroma. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Duyaya (Belviz No. 901) durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Duyaya the same as Duyaya (Belviz No. 901)?
items.a: Yes. Duyaya is another name for Duyaya (Belviz No. 901), registered as NSIC 1999 Dr 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 45 to 50 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Duyaya (Belviz No. 901)?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
